title: A study to test whether a nasal antibody spray can help reduce flu infection in healthy adults, using a controlled research setting where volunteers are exposed to flu under medical supervision
official: A phase 2a, single-center, two-part, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of intranasally administered CR9114 monoclonal antibody in healthy adults in a human influenza challenge model
summary:
Background and study aims
Influenza (flu) illness affects millions of people every year despite available vaccines. Flu vaccine effectiveness averages around 50% because of vaccine strains not matching flu strains in the community. CR9114 is an antibody that is being developed to prevent flu illness regardless of flu strains.

This study is testing CR9114 nasal spray antibody in healthy adults. The study will look at whether the spray is safe, how it behaves in the body, and whether it can help reduce flu infection.

CR9114 nasal spray has been studied in 175 healthy adults without clinical concerns. No allergic reactions were observed. Anti-drug antibodies were observed in 1/175 participants, which was already present at baseline, and without any clinical consequences

Who can participate?
Healthy adults aged 18 to 55 years who fit the specific study criteria will be invited to take part.

What does the study involve?
Participants who are eligible to take part will be randomly assigned to receive either CR9114 or a placebo nasal spray (a spray without active medicine). Neither the participant nor the study team will know which treatment has been given. 

Participants will stay as in-patient in a specialized clinical research unit for 12-13 days and will be closely monitored by experienced medical staff throughout the study. Total participation is approximately 5 months.

The study has two parts:
In both Part A and Part B, participants will receive CR9114 or placebo nasal spray for 10 days to see if the spray is safe and tolerated, and how it works in the body. During the study, blood and nasal samples will be taken which could cause discomfort.

In Part B only, participants will take part in a carefully controlled research model where they are given a flu virus under close medical supervision. This allows researchers to understand whether the nasal spray can help reduce flu infection. Controlled inoculation is necessary to test efficacy in a reproducible, closely supervised setting. Symptoms of flu typically include runny nose, congestion, fever, malaise, muscle aches, and sore throat, usually resolving within 3–7 days.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
It is not known if there will be any benefits from joining this study. The researchers are trying to see if CR9114 can improve flu prevention. CR9114 has been studied in 3 studies with good safety profile. The specific flu challenge virus has been safely administered by hVIVO without clinical concerns.  

Where is the study run from?
The study is sponsored by Leyden Laboratories B.V. and will take place at hVIVO, a specialist influenza research unit in the United Kingdom.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 to March 2027.

Who is funding the study?
Leyden Laboratories B.V. (Netherlands)

conditions: Healthy volunteers. Intended indication for CR9114 monoclonal antibody under development: prevention (prophylaxis) of influenza A and B infections in adults.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Written informed consent signed and dated by the participant and the PI/investigator obtained before any assessment is performed
2. Aged between 18 and 55 years old on the day prior to signing the consent form
3. Total body weight ≥50 kg and BMI ≥18 kg/m² and ≤35 kg/m²
4. In good health with no history or current evidence of clinically significant medical conditions
5. Females of non-childbearing potential or females of childbearing potential with negative pregnancy test and use of highly effective contraceptive method from 2 weeks before first study visit until 28 days after last IMP dose
6. Serosuitable for the challenge agent (Part B only): serology indicating susceptibility to influenza A/H1N1 challenge virus
Exclusion criteria:
1. History of or currently active symptoms of upper or lower respiratory tract infection within 4 weeks prior to first study visit
2. Any clinically significant or active disease that may interfere with study participation per PI or investigator
3. Current smoker, or ex-smoker who ceased within the past 6 months, or cumulative smoking history ≥10 pack-years including significant vaping history
4. Females who are breastfeeding, have been pregnant within 6 months prior to the study
5. Lifetime history of anaphylaxis or severe allergic reaction, or significant food or drug intolerance in the last 12 months
6. Significant anatomical nasal abnormality, clinically significant epistaxis within 3 months
7. Within 180 days prior to viral challenge: receipt of influenza vaccine or antiviral medication for influenza or have confirmed influenza illness
8. Receipt of any vaccination within 4 weeks prior to first IMP dose, or intention to receive vaccination before end of follow-up
9. Receipt of any investigational drug within 3 months prior to first IMP dose
10. Immunomodulatory drugs or systemic or intranasal corticosteroids within 6 months prior to first IMP dose, systemic antivirals within 4 weeks, or chronic intranasal medications within 3 months
11. Positive HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C test
12. Positive drug screen on admission
